title: How many faces, edges and vertices has a ten sided prism?
description: A prism has two congruent polygons with ten sides as its opposite faces. The video counts its faces, edges and vertices and then writes the counts for a polygon with n sides. Keeko's doubt is that the prism has twenty edges.
teaching_notes: One idea: a prism on an n sided polygon has n plus two faces, three n edges and two n vertices. Watch for students who count only the edges of the two polygons.

source: A prism has two congruent 10 sided polygons as opposite face
video_script.why: The child has counted the parts of a triangular prism and now counts them for a prism on a polygon with ten sides, then with n sides.
video_script.substitution: Count the faces, edges and vertices from the two polygons and the parts that join them, then write the same counts for n sides.
video_script.anchor: a prism standing on a polygon with ten sides, with a matching polygon on top
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts only the edges of the two polygons, ten and ten, and says the prism has twenty edges. Ten more edges join the matching corners of the two polygons, so the prism has thirty edges.
video_script.payoff_line: The prism has twelve faces, thirty edges and twenty vertices

final_answer.value: 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices; for n sides, n + 2 faces, 3n edges and 2n vertices
final_answer.spoken: twelve faces, thirty edges and twenty vertices; for n sides, n plus two faces, three n edges and two n vertices

hold_back: Answer: 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices; for n sides, n + 2 faces, 3n edges and 2n vertices
maths_rules: for n sides: n + 2 faces, 3n edges, 2n vertices
slip: counting only the edges of the polygons gives 20 edges
video_script.design: A prism on a ten sided polygon stands on the stage; faces, edges and vertices glow in turn with the count beside each, and then the counts are rewritten with n.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a prism standing on a polygon with ten sides, with a matching polygon on top; labels faces, edges and vertices each with a question mark

marks.book: the title card and the prism appear
marks.ask: the three labels appear with question marks
marks.more: the number 10 on the polygon changes to n

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about prisms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A prism has two congruent polygons with ten sides as its opposite faces. How many faces, edges and vertices does it have?
<bookmark mark='more'/>What if the polygons have n sides?

beats.on_screen: the prism and the three labels stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two congruent polygons facing each other; edges drawn between matching corners; the side faces shaded as parallelograms

marks.def: the two congruent polygons appear as opposite faces
marks.join: edges are drawn between the matching corners
marks.side: the side faces are shaded as parallelograms

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>A prism has two congruent polygons as its opposite faces.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Edges connect the matching corners of these two polygons.
<bookmark mark='side'/>All the other faces are parallelograms, one for each side of the polygon.

beats.on_screen: Given: prism with two congruent polygons of 10 sides as opposite faces

marks.given: the two polygons are labelled 10 sides on the prism

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a prism has two congruent polygons with ten sides as opposite faces.

beats.on_screen: To find: faces, edges, vertices, for 10 sides and for n sides

marks.find: the words faces, edges and vertices are written with 10 sides and n sides

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the faces, edges and vertices, first for ten sides and then for n sides.
<bookmark mark='para'/>Step one, count the faces. Each of the ten sides of the polygon gives one parallelogram, so there are ten of them.
<bookmark mark='poly'/>The two polygons add two more faces.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Ten plus two is twelve faces.

beats.on_screen: Edges: 10 on each polygon and 10 joining them: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30

marks.polys: the ten edges of each polygon glow
marks.join: the ten joining edges glow and 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='polys'/>Step two, count the edges. Each polygon has ten edges, so the two polygons have ten and ten.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Ten more edges join the matching corners. Ten plus ten plus ten is thirty edges.

marks.corners: the ten corners of each polygon are marked with dots

narration: <bookmark mark='corners'/>Step three, count the vertices. Each polygon has ten corners, and the joining edges add no new ones.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Ten plus ten is twenty vertices.

beats.on_screen: For n sides: faces n + 2, edges 3n, vertices 2n. Put n = 10: 12, 30, 20.

marks.rule: n + 2, 3n and 2n are written in place of the counts
marks.check: n = 10 is put in and 12, 30 and 20 are written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, do the same counting for n sides. The faces are n plus two, the edges are three n, and the vertices are two n.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Put n equal to ten, and the counts match the ones above.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices; for n sides, n + 2 faces, 3n edges and 2n vertices

marks.gen: the counts for n sides are written under the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The prism has twelve faces, thirty edges and twenty vertices.
<bookmark mark='gen'/>For n sides, it has n plus two faces, three n edges and two n vertices.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the prism
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 10 + 10 = 20 edges, struck through; the ten joining edges glow on the prism

marks.doubt: the bubble with 10 + 10 = 20 appears beside the prism
marks.join: the ten joining edges glow on the prism
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 30 edges returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the prism has twenty edges, because each polygon has ten edges.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Look at the prism again. Ten more edges join the corners of one polygon to the matching corners of the other.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Those edges count too, so the prism has thirty edges.
